title: Optical Overlay Metrology - Scratches Detection on Puma 9900
subtitle: Post-Planarization Quality Validation for 7nm Node Manufacturing
author: Maria Gonzalez

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Puma 9900 system to detect and classify Scratches defects during post-planarization inspection at the 7nm technology node. The test is conducted at Chandler Fab 42 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 450mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Scratches defects that are critical to yield at the 7nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Puma 9900 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Puma 9900
- Inspection Type: Optical Overlay Metrology
- Target Defect: Scratches
- Process Step: Post-Planarization
- Wafer Size: 450mm
- Technology Node: 7nm
- Fab Location: Chandler Fab 42

This test case applies to all Puma 9900 systems deployed at Chandler Fab 42 for post-planarization monitoring in the 7nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Puma 9900
Software Version: v8.7.463
Recipe: OPTICAL_OVERLAY_METROLOGY_7nm_POST_PLANARIZATION
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: High (177 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.5μm
Edge Exclusion: 4mm
Sampling Plan: 5-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Puma 9900 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Optical Overlay Metrology' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Scratches defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 7nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 83 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 98% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±0.7% for Optical Overlay Metrology
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.94 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-02-14
Wafers Tested: 11
Total Defects Found: 4583
Defect Density: 1458.82 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 3.1%
Capture Rate: 96.6%
Test Duration: 381 minutes
System Uptime: 96.0%

Result Classification: FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Puma 9900 demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Scratches at the 7nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Cross-correlation with the reference SEM confirmed classification accuracy.

e) SECS/GEM communication was verified with zero packet loss during data transfer.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Re-tune detection algorithm thresholds for Scratches at 7nm node.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Escalate to R&D for algorithm enhancement if re-tuning does not resolve sensitivity gap.
